title: Weekly Markets Monitor - Unwedged
gist: In the week to 7 August 2026, gold in US dollars broke out of the wedge that had confined it since January between a series of lower highs and a technical floor at US$4,000, driven by broad-based gold ETF buying with Asian-hours trading leading price action. The World Gold Council attributes the move to a weak non-farm payrolls print (whose signal it doubts), yen intervention and progress toward a Middle East resolution, alongside lower US Treasury yields and a softer dollar. Note the published web page is dated 10 August 2026 while the underlying data is as of 7 August 2026, and the detailed analysis sits in a downloadable PDF rather than this text.

insights.claim: Gold priced in US dollars has broken out of the wedge pattern formed by a series of lower highs since January 2026 and a technical floor around US$4,000 that had repeatedly held.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: A confirmed break of a multi-month consolidation removes the overhead lower-high resistance; treat US$4,000 as the reference level that must now hold on any retest.
insights.quote: gold in US$ has broken free of the wedge formed by lower highs since January and a resilient technical floor at the US$4,000 level

insights.claim: The gold breakout was driven by broad-based gold ETF buying rather than a single regional bid, with Asian trading hours leading the price action.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: Asian-hours leadership plus ETF inflows points to real allocation demand rather than futures-led short covering; watch daily ETF holdings and Asian session opens for follow-through.
insights.quote: Helped by broad-based gold ETF buying but with Asian hours leading price action

insights.claim: The World Gold Council flags this breakout as its Chart of the Week, titled 'Unwedged', with data as of 7 August 2026 sourced from Bloomberg and its own analysis.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: The house view is being anchored on a technical regime change in gold, which typically precedes more constructive WGC demand commentary.

themes.theme: Payrolls signal doubted, Fed repricing modest

insights.claim: A weak US non-farm payrolls print contributed to the gold move, but doubts about the reliability of that signal, given seasonal distortions and firm jobless claims data, limited how much markets repriced the Federal Reserve path.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: Gold rallied on a rate-cut impulse that rates markets only partially bought; if subsequent claims and payrolls confirm the cooling, there is unspent Fed-repricing fuel for gold, and if they do not, the rally loses one of its legs.
insights.quote: Weak non-farm payrolls may have played a part, but doubts over the signal, given seasonal distortions and firm claims data, kept Fed repricing modest.

insights.claim: Within the US economy, resilient business activity and strong corporate earnings are running against a cooling labour market, an internally uneven picture rather than a clean slowdown.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: The activity-versus-labour split is the key ambiguity for Fed timing; conflicting prints keep both equity and gold bulls alive and argue for holding both rather than choosing.
insights.quote: resilient business activity and strong corporate earnings contrasted with a cooling labour market

insights.claim: Over the week major global equity markets advanced while oil prices eased and both US Treasury yields and the US dollar moved lower.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: Lower real-rate and dollar backdrop is the classic tailwind combination for gold; equities and gold rising together signals liquidity/rates relief rather than risk aversion.
insights.quote: Major global equity markets advanced, while oil prices eased and both US Treasury yields and the US dollar moved lower.

insights.claim: Japanese yen intervention and incremental progress towards a Middle East resolution are cited as probable additional contributors to the week's gold move, meaning the rally had FX and geopolitical legs alongside the rates story.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: A multi-driver rally is more durable than a single-catalyst one, but it also means gold gives back gains if any one leg reverses; monitor yen intervention follow-through and Hormuz headlines.
insights.quote: Yen intervention and an inching towards a Middle East resolution probably contributed too.

insights.claim: Geopolitical concerns eased over the week as talks on securing access through the Strait of Hormuz continued.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: Easing Hormuz risk is consistent with the softer oil price and removes a safe-haven bid, which makes the simultaneous gold breakout more notable as a rates/flow-driven move than a fear trade.
insights.quote: Geopolitical concerns eased as talks on access through the Strait of Hormuz continued.

insights.claim: Gold broke out in the same week that geopolitical risk eased and oil fell, an unusual combination since safe-haven de-escalation would normally weigh on the metal.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: Gold strength without a geopolitical bid suggests the marginal buyer is allocation-driven (ETFs, rates, dollar) and that the move is less vulnerable to a Middle East peace deal than headlines imply.

insights.claim: Economic updates were uneven across major economies during the week, with no synchronised global growth signal to anchor on.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: Divergent regional data supports relative-value and FX trades over directional global macro bets, and keeps central bank paths desynchronised.
insights.quote: Economic updates were uneven across major economies

insights.claim: Eurozone manufacturing improved over the period, one of the few clear positive regional data points in the week.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: Improving euro-area manufacturing argues against further ECB easing urgency and is a mild support for the euro against the weakening dollar.

insights.claim: China's exports stayed strong even as its domestic activity moderated, while Japan's consumer spending weakened further.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: Export-led Chinese resilience with soft domestic demand keeps stimulus expectations alive, while weakening Japanese consumption complicates the BoJ's normalisation and interacts with the yen intervention story.
insights.quote: China’s exports stayed strong even as domestic activity moderated

insights.claim: In India, the Reserve Bank of India kept policy rates unchanged while business activity moderated.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: An on-hold RBI with softening activity matters for the world's second-largest gold consumer: stable rates and a softer dollar are supportive for Indian physical demand into the festival season.
insights.quote: in India, the RBI kept rates unchanged while business activity moderated
